Spoken
Madam Vice President, we honor you,
Verse 1 (praise)
First woman to rise, to lead, to see it through.
A teacher of teachers, a builder of minds,
You opened the doors for the girls left behind.
From the lecture hall to the seat you hold,
Your story is written in letters of gold.
And now we come with a different plea,
Verse 2 (plea)
Not for degrees, but for our land, you see.
The women who farm from dawn to dark,
The children who wonder where the good soil went.
They look to you, Madam, they look to you,
Their hope is a hope only you can renew.
Madam Vice President, hear our call,
Chorus
Ghana is waiting, waiting for all.
The land is tired, the land needs you,
Rise for the soil, rise for what's true!
We are Acres, we plead today,
Ghana is waiting for what you'll say.
The ancestors are watching from beyond,
Verse 3
The earth herself is asking to respond.
She gave us the soil, she gave us the yield,
Now she is tired, now she is healed
Only by hands that will not delay,
Madam, the time is now, not another day.
Asaase Yaa is calling your name,
Mother Earth Ghana will not be the same.
When the seventieth year of our freedom is told,
Verse 4 (legacy)
When the story of Ghana's land is retold,
Let it be said, in that chapter, of you,
"She stood for the soil, and she saw it through."
Your children's children will speak your name,
Not just for office, but for what you became.
Madam Vice President, hear our call,
